s1.syndrome_frame: Subcutaneous swellings with progressive enlargement over months, firm to hard, without pain, and with normal overlying skin
salient_findings: Bilateral neck masses and masses on the back and anterior abdominal wall
Firm to hard, nontender, mobile swellings
Cytology showing plump spindle cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm
key_facts: 15-year-old girl presented with multiple swellings
Swellings have been progressively enlarging over five months
No pain associated with the swellings
Seven subcutaneous swellings were found on examination
Swellings were firm to hard and mobile
No changes in the overlying skin
Normal complete blood count, metabolic panel, and skeletal survey
FNAC showed moderate cellularity with similar features at all sites
Cytology smears showed predominantly plump spindle cells
Ultrasonography confirmed lesions were confined to subcutaneous tissue
No lymphadenopathy or deeper masses were found

differentials: Hyalinizing spindle cell tumor with giant rosettes
per_call: Hyalinizing spindle cell tumor with giant rosettes

shortlist.label: Desmoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of firm, mobile subcutaneous swellings without pain

shortlist.label: Fibromatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to desmoid tumor, with progressive enlargement of subcutaneous masses

shortlist.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by firm, subcutaneous nodules with progressive growth

shortlist.label: Nodular fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presents as a rapidly growing, firm subcutaneous nodule

shortlist.label: Spindle cell lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cytology showing spindle cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm is consistent with this diagnosis
